html:
How to add a Skill

A new skill adds deterministic tools to the model's available actions. It must not add another semantic decision owner.

  1. Create src/agent_runtime/skills/<skill_id>/ with __init__.py, skill.py, owned tools/services and focused tests. Keep shared transport, persistence and runtime infrastructure outside the skill.
  2. Define source-owned ToolDefinition instances with globally unique IDs, complete argument schemas, accurate result documentation and conservative effects.
  3. Implement handlers returning ExecutionResult from actual provider/OS observations. Receive services through explicit dependencies or authorized execution context. Enforce target scope, platform and credentials there.
  4. Create a SkillDefinition grouping those tools and describing prerequisites. Declare progress support explicitly; use SkillProgressDefinition.unavailable() with a reason when no detailed extractor exists. For tools with optional services, attach a deterministic availability_check(context) that returns {"available": false, "reason": "..."} when the service or required local dependency is absent. Return authentication_required or configuration_required separately when a present service needs sign-in or a profile. Use local checks, without inference or provider mutations.
  5. Define build_skill(registry: CapabilityRegistry) -> SkillDefinition in skill.py and export it from the package. Add one explicit factory entry to skills/catalog.py::SKILL_FACTORIES, after any tools referenced by uses_tools. Registry/catalog discovery handles schema exposure; packages are never scanned or auto-registered. The registry argument gives configurable skills the existing configuration store.
  6. Test discovery and availability, arguments, authorization, execution, receipts, scope isolation, exact result chaining and uncertain external effects.
from agent_runtime.execution.models import ExecutionResult
from agent_runtime.capabilities.registry import CapabilityRegistry
from agent_runtime.progress.contracts import SkillProgressDefinition
from agent_runtime.tools import SkillDefinition, ToolDefinition, object_schema


# Test/example only: do not ship an echo tool as a product skill.
def echo(arguments, context):
    return ExecutionResult(
        operation_id=context["operation_id"],
        status="success",
        data_preview={"response": {"value": arguments["value"]}},
    )


def build_skill(registry: CapabilityRegistry) -> SkillDefinition:
    return SkillDefinition(
        skill_id="test",
        display_name="Echo fixture",
        description="Test-only example",
        tools=(
            ToolDefinition(
                id="test.echo",
                display_name="Echo",
                description="Return the supplied value",
                effect="read",
                arguments_schema=object_schema({"value": {"type": "string"}}, ["value"]),
                executor=echo,
            ),
        ),
        progress=SkillProgressDefinition.unavailable(
            "This synchronous example has no intermediate progress evidence."
        ),
    )

Tools that accept exact references can declare input_bindings with execution.bindings.BINDINGS_SCHEMA and an inputs object. Bindings supply exact values before the executor runs. If an adapter can launch durable jobs, integrate with the existing job identity and cancellation contract.

Every advertised argument must work as documented; test its observable effect and reject irrelevant action-specific options. result_schema describes result data and is checked by adapter contract tests. The adapter owns successful output validation and normalization. The generic executor does not turn a post-effect schema mismatch into evidence that the operation never executed. See the tool contract guide for the complete availability and result semantics.

Do not modify the model's core loop to add a skill. Do not add a sub-agent or semantic routing. Ordinary skills require no edits to completion, persistence or output formatting. A new skill must not import AgentLoop.

Guidance-only skills may declare tools=(), uses_tools=("python.run",) and concise instructions. Referenced tools must already be registered. The catalog includes the instructions in those tools' existing model descriptions and resolves skill discovery to the same tools. An optional local availability_check(context) can report prerequisite state; unavailable skills contribute the reason rather than execution instructions. This adds no routing inference or tool invocation. Tool ownership, execution authorization and receipts stay with the original tool. Skills with longer shared guidance can set the source-only instructions_once=True flag. The catalog attaches that guidance to the first allowed advertised tool; existing skills retain their default per-tool behavior. Memory uses this to keep proactive learning instructions capability-scoped without repeating them per tool. Excluding a guidance skill hides its instructions; excluding its underlying tool removes execution access as usual. The Visualization skill is the production example.

tests/test_v55_skill_contract.py is the executable example. Its test-only Echo skill is discovered, called by a scripted model, executed by the production engine, persisted as receipts, chained with JSON Pointer into another tool, read, and checked at completion.

tests/test_v55_final_cleanup.py covers missing services, platform restrictions, new-skill availability, descriptive result schemas and compatibility boundaries.

Generated APIs and private connection profiles

Use entry_tool_ids for the common domain operations of a large API and SkillSectionDefinition for its source hierarchy. Keep discovery non-recursive, validate ownership/cycles and use deterministic generated descriptors with one executor factory. The Proxmox package is the production example: its four entries coordinate guest resolution and task waits internally while advanced operations are discovered by section. See discovery and Proxmox source generation.

Set default_enabled=false for an optional integration and preserve the existing policy envelope when promoting entries from typed parameters. Select the appropriate cancellation_transport when reusing Gateway HTTP. A domain client must use the existing transport, ordinary ask_user and approval boundaries.

JSON templates belong in parameters/templates.py and prefill the shared editor. Recognized private profiles need strict save validation, an allowlisted model projection and exact accepted revision bindings. Never put credentials into Working Context. A new Working Context adapter implements validate, project, supersedes, check_target and GUIDANCE; colocate it with its skill and register it in skills/catalog.py::working_context_adapters. Non-skill resource adapters belong in native/resource_adapters/. Test a real Conversation-mode follow-up. Register volatile cleanup through native/conversation_resources.py when the state belongs to a conversation.

Document the file and significant symbols under the source standard, classify new operational scripts and data, and add a README.md explaining each new folder's immediate files and child folders. The audit discovers tracked and nonignored unstaged files during review; update scope/classification rules when the new material needs a different category. Refresh inventories with scripts/refresh_directory_guides.py --write and inspect the resulting prose. The tool contract guide owns the complete field, progress and resource-classification reference.
